evals.prompt: I run a dental clinic in Halandri (Χαλάνδρι), in the northern suburbs of Athens. Most of my patients come from Halandri, Marousi and Vrilissia. Services: general dentistry, dental implants, and teeth whitening. My website is 5 pages, all in Greek, and I have a verified Google Business Profile that I have never posted to. I have no SEO tools connected and no keyword data to give you. Which keywords should I target to get more local patients, and where exactly does each one belong?
evals.expected_output: A Greek local-market keyword research report: Greek seed keywords expanded through the Step 4 dual-coverage table (accented Greek / unaccented Greek / Greeklish / EN equivalent) with placement noted per form; intent classification and difficulty per keyword with every volume figure openly marked as estimated; local-intent keywords mapped to Google Business Profile surfaces (Products/Services descriptions, Q&A) in addition to website pages; prioritized quick wins appropriate for a small 5-page local site.
expectations: Greek seed keywords (e.g., οδοντίατρος Χαλάνδρι, λεύκανση δοντιών, εμφυτεύματα δοντιών) are expanded in a dual-coverage table where each seed shows all four forms of SKILL.md Step 4 — (a) accented Greek, (b) unaccented Greek, (c) Greeklish transliteration, (d) EN equivalent — with no form missing.

Placement is stated per form and matches references/greek-keyword-coverage.md: only accented Greek is recommended for visible copy (titles, H1s, body, meta, alt text); unaccented Greek gets no visible-copy placement ('Do not write it into visible copy'); Greeklish is confined to domains, brand variants, and paid search bids — not body text.

At least one service+city/area keyword is mapped to the GBP Products/Services description, and at least one question query (e.g., πόσο κοστίζει η λεύκανση δοντιών) is mapped to GBP Q&A with the instruction to proactively seed the top 3-5 questions (any count inside that range satisfies it — seeding exactly 5 passes) — per SKILL.md Step 10 and the Output Validation item 'Local-intent keywords mapped to GBP surfaces, not just website pages'.

The report never recommends creating a separate page for an unaccented or Greeklish spelling variant, and never recommends meta-keywords or hidden-text variant placement — the reference labels one-page-per-variant a 'thin-content/doorway-page pattern and a ranking risk' and hidden-text variant stuffing a spam violation.

Every keyword row carries volume, difficulty, and intent — per the Output Validation items 'Every keyword analysis table (incl. GEO/conversational and local) carries volume / difficulty / intent columns' and 'Keywords grouped by intent and mapped to content types'; where a metric is not tool-reported, an explained N/A cell (e.g. 'N/A — no tool connected') passes, while an invented number fails; placement/crosswalk tables (e.g. the Step-10 GBP mapping) are exempt from carrying the columns only when every keyword they reference already has a metricized analysis row — a keyword target first introduced in a crosswalk with no analysis row above fails.

Because no SEO tool is connected and the user supplied no data, every volume and difficulty figure is explicitly labeled estimated (or unavailable); no figure is presented as tool-sourced — per the Output Validation item 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, user-provided, or estimated)'.

evals.prompt: geia! exw ena mikro eshop me xeiropoiita kosmimata — asimenia daxtylidia kai skoularikia. poulaw kyriws apo instagram alla thelw na me vriskoun kai sto google. den exw kanena seo ergaleio. ti lexeis-kleidia na valw? na grapsw kai sta agglika i sta greeklish mesa sto site gia na me vriskoun oloi?
evals.expected_output: A Greek-market keyword plan that treats the Greeklish prompt as Greek demand: seeds rendered in accented Greek (χειροποίητα κοσμήματα, ασημένια δαχτυλίδια, χειροποίητα σκουλαρίκια), the 4-form dual-coverage table per seed with 2-3 plausible Greeklish variants where transliteration is ambiguous, intent classification and topic clustering for an e-commerce niche, all volumes marked estimated, and a direct answer to the user's question: Greeklish belongs in domains/brand/paid search — not in visible shop copy — while EN forms belong on EN-audience pages only.
expectations: The Greeklish prompt is recognized as a Greek-market request: seed keywords are rendered in accented Greek script (e.g., χειροποίητα κοσμήματα, ασημένια δαχτυλίδια), not researched only in Latin characters.
Each Greek seed appears with all four forms of the Step 4 dual-coverage pattern present: accented Greek, unaccented Greek, Greeklish, and EN equivalent.

For at least one seed containing χ (e.g., χειροποίητα), the Greeklish form offers 2-3 plausible transliteration variants (e.g., xeiropoiita / cheiropoiita) — per the reference instruction to 'generate 2-3 plausible variants per keyword (e.g., both "x" and "h" for χ) rather than assuming one canonical spelling'.

The user's question about writing Greeklish inside the site is answered per the placement rule: Greeklish is NOT recommended for visible shop copy (the reference says it 'reads as unprofessional / spam-adjacent to native readers'); it is confined to domains/URL slugs, brand-name and social-handle variants, and paid-search keyword lists.
EN-equivalent forms are assigned to EN-audience content (bilingual/international-facing pages) as a genuinely different audience segment — not mixed into the Greek pages as extra spelling variants.

Keywords are classified by intent (transactional/commercial product terms vs informational queries) and grouped into topic clusters mapped to content types — with at least one named pillar that has at least 2 cluster items grouped under it.
All volume figures are explicitly labeled estimated or unavailable — none presented as tool data, since the user said no SEO tool is connected.

The 4 forms of each seed are scored as one aggregated demand cluster in opportunity scoring, not as four separate keywords — per the reference: 'sum estimated/known volume across all 4 forms when scoring opportunity (Step 7) — they represent one underlying need'.

evals.prompt: We're a UK digital agency and we've just signed a car rental company in Heraklion, Crete ('Minoan Wheels'). Nobody on our team reads Greek. I've attached the client brief and the keyword export from our Ahrefs trial. Build the Greek-market keyword strategy: what should the planned Greek pages target, what stays on the English site, and what belongs on their Google Business Profile? Also flag anything in our export that we're likely misreading as non-Greek speakers.
evals.expected_output: A bilingual Greek-market keyword strategy that labels the Ahrefs export rows as tool-sourced, spots that the accented/unaccented/Greeklish export rows are spelling variants of one demand cluster and aggregates their volumes for opportunity scoring, expands seeds through the 4-form dual-coverage table, assigns accented Greek to the planned Greek pages and EN equivalents to the English tourist-facing site, maps local-intent keywords to GBP surfaces (empty Services section, unseeded Q&A), and prioritizes using the skill's opportunity formula.
expectations: Figures taken from the attached CSV are labeled as tool-sourced/user-provided (Ahrefs export), and any keyword added beyond the export has its volume explicitly marked estimated — the two sources are never blended without labels, per the Output Validation item 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, user-provided, or estimated)'.

The export rows 'ενοικίαση αυτοκινήτου κρήτη' (1900), 'ενοικιαση αυτοκινητου κρητη' (1300), and 'enoikiasi aftokinitou kriti' (210) are explicitly identified as spelling variants of one keyword, and their volumes are aggregated into a single demand cluster for opportunity scoring rather than treated as three independent keywords — per the reference: 'sum estimated/known volume across all 4 forms when scoring opportunity (Step 7)'.

Greek seeds are expanded through the Step 4 dual-coverage artifact: a single table in which each seed's row contains all four forms — accented Greek, unaccented Greek, Greeklish, EN equivalent — written out as literal keyword strings (not merely referenced or described), with a placement recommendation stated per form; this table is required even though the keywords arrived via a tool export.

The strategy assigns accented-Greek forms to the visible copy of the planned Greek pages and EN-equivalent keywords (e.g., car rental crete, car hire heraklion airport) to the English site for the tourist audience — and does not recommend separate pages for unaccented or Greeklish spellings, which the reference calls a 'thin-content/doorway-page pattern and a ranking risk'.

Local-intent keywords are mapped to GBP surfaces per SKILL.md Step 10: at minimum one service+location keyword to the (currently empty) Products/Services description, and the question query 'πόσο κοστίζει ενοικίαση αυτοκινήτου στην κρήτη' to GBP Q&A with the top 3-5 questions seeded proactively.
Prioritization applies the skill's formula Opportunity = (Volume × Intent Value) / Difficulty with the intent weights Informational=1, Navigational=1, Commercial=2, Transactional=3.

Every keyword row shows volume, difficulty, and intent columns; placement/crosswalk tables (e.g. the Step-10 GBP mapping) are exempt from carrying the columns only when every keyword they reference already has a metricized analysis row — a keyword target first introduced in a crosswalk with no analysis row above fails.

evals.prompt: I'm the solo founder of a bootstrapped SaaS that automates invoice reconciliation for small US accounting firms. The domain is 8 months old with roughly DA 12. I have no SEO tools connected and no keyword data of my own. Goal is demo signups. Which keywords should I go after first, and in what order?
evals.expected_output: A prioritized keyword plan: seeds expanded to long-tail variants, every keyword classified by intent and clustered under a named pillar, difficulty judged against the weak DA-12 domain, ordering derived from the skill's opportunity formula with low-difficulty quick wins first, question/definition keywords flagged as GEO opportunities, and all metrics openly labeled estimated since no tool or user data exists.
expectations: Every keyword — including every row of the GEO/AI-citation opportunities table, which is not exempt — is classified into one of the skill's four intent categories — informational, navigational, commercial, transactional — per SKILL.md Step 5; a format/'Type' label on GEO rows does not substitute for an intent category.

Keywords are grouped into at least one topic cluster with a named pillar and cluster items that link back to the pillar — per the Output Validation item 'Topic clusters show clear pillar-to-cluster relationships'.

Ordering applies the skill's formula Opportunity = (Volume × Intent Value) / Difficulty (intent weights: Informational=1, Navigational=1, Commercial=2, Transactional=3), and the first-priority picks are low-difficulty quick wins consistent with a DA-12, 8-month-old domain.

All volume and difficulty figures are explicitly labeled estimated (or unavailable) — none is presented as measured tool data, per the Output Validation item 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, user-provided, or estimated)'.

Every keyword row — including every row of the GEO/AI-citation opportunities table, which is not exempt — includes volume, difficulty, and intent columns, per the Output Validation item 'Every keyword analysis table (incl. GEO/conversational and local) carries volume / difficulty / intent columns'; where a metric is not tool-reported, an explained N/A cell passes, while an invented number fails.
Question-format or definition keywords (e.g., 'what is invoice reconciliation') are flagged as GEO/AI-citation opportunities per SKILL.md Step 8.

evals.prompt: We sell project management software for construction teams. Pull every keyword that monday.com and asana.com currently rank for that our site (buildtrack.io) doesn't, with their ranking URLs and positions, so we can close the gap one page at a time.
evals.expected_output: The response recognizes this as a competitor keyword-gap request and points to the competitor-analysis skill per this skill's own description boundary, passing along handoff context (buildtrack.io plus the two competitor domains). It does not fabricate competitor rankings, positions, or URLs, and anything it does offer stays inside keyword-research's own scope (seed and intent research for construction PM software), clearly framed as such rather than as the requested gap report.
expectations: The response explicitly names competitor-analysis as the correct skill for a competitor keyword-gap breakdown, consistent with the skill description's boundary 'For competitor keyword gaps, see competitor-analysis' and the Related Skills entry 'competitor-analysis — See what keywords competitors rank for'.

No fabricated competitor data: the response does not present specific keywords, positions, or ranking URLs attributed to monday.com or asana.com as observed fact without tool data; any competitor keyword guesses are labeled as assumptions or estimates. Hedged common-knowledge characterizations of competitor rankings (e.g. 'monday.com likely ranks for broad project-management terms') count as fabrication unless explicitly labeled as an assumption or estimate — hedging words alone ('likely', 'probably') are not such a label.
The referral carries handoff context for competitor-analysis — at minimum the user's domain (buildtrack.io) and both competitor domains — per the library's inter-skill handoff convention.

Any interim keyword work offered stays within this skill's scope (seed expansion / intent classification for the user's own topic, with sources labeled) and is not presented as the requested competitor gap report.
